youtube_title: The keeper's son: Lake Michigan took his parents, then he helped keep Michigan City's pier light
youtube:
In 1878, South Manitou Island's lighthouse keeper, Aaron Sheridan, his wife and assistant keeper, Julia, and their baby son, Robert, were coming home from the mainland in a small boat. Within a mile of the island it overturned in icy water. A fisherman with them was rescued; the Sheridans drowned, and the lake never gave them back. Their five other sons were sent to grandparents in Illinois. One of them, George, grew up to keep lights too: in 1905 he became first assistant keeper of Michigan City's new East Pierhead Light, and another Sheridan ran that light until 1930. Comment your town, and it could be next! #MichiganCity #LakeMichigan #Lighthouse #Indiana #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn; no people are shown in the boat or the water. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: National Park Service, Sleeping Bear Dunes (Aaron Sheridan; South Manitou Island Cemetery); Dianna Stampfler, PromoteMichigan (from her book Michigan's Haunted Lighthouses), quoting the Chicago Tribune of March 19, 1878; Lighthousefriends (South Manitou Island, Michigan City, Kalamazoo River); Lighthouse Digest; U.S. Lighthouse Society archives (Register of Lighthouse Keepers); Terry Pepper, Seeing the Light; U.S. Coast Guard History; National Register of Historic Places nomination; Old Lighthouse Museum, Michigan City. More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history

Michigan City's pier light, and the keeper's son.
In 1878, Aaron Sheridan kept the lighthouse on South Manitou Island, up the lake. His wife, Julia, was his assistant keeper.
On March 15, 1878, they were coming home from the mainland in a small boat with their baby son, Robert, and a fisherman. Within a mile of the island, it overturned in icy water. The fisherman was rescued. The Sheridans drowned, and the lake never gave them back. Their five other sons were sent to grandparents in Illinois.
One of them, George, grew up to keep lights too. In 1905, he became first assistant keeper of Michigan City's new East Pierhead Light. Another Sheridan ran that light until 1930.

factcheck: Independent fact-check Nov. 15, 2026: not ready on first pass; fixed before posting. Cut the tower-watching line (Lighthousefriends: the boys ran up and down the beach), 'kept' to 'helped keep' (George was first assistant), Phillip/Philip spelled both ways so the narration says 'another Sheridan', island light drawn dark while both keepers were in the boat, the 1905 pier building darkened (National Register: painted buff until about 1920), Find a Grave dropped from the credits. 1905 rests on Lighthouse Digest ('on April 1, 1905, George became the 1st assistant keeper') and the USLHS Register; Terry Pepper agrees (four years as first assistant).
